findings.title: Use the account UI's interpolation syntax
findings.body: This catalog uses `{{...}}` placeholders (for example, `backTo=Back to {{app}}`), but this message was changed to Java `MessageFormat` placeholders and a Java `choice` expression. The account UI will not interpolate these values or evaluate the choice, so users will see literal braces instead of the attribute name and configured size limits in validation errors.

findings.title: Use the admin UI's interpolation syntax
findings.body: This admin UI catalog previously used `{{0}}`, `{{1}}`, and `{{2}}` placeholders, but this replacement uses Java `MessageFormat` and `choice` syntax. The frontend will not substitute the attribute or limits, leaving users with literal formatting tokens in the multivalued-attribute validation error.

findings.title: The Lithuanian OTP instruction is in Italian
findings.body: The changed `totpStep1` value reads “Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare,” which is Italian rather than Lithuanian. Lithuanian account users will see an unrelated-language instruction during authenticator setup.

findings.title: The Lithuanian OTP instruction is in Italian
findings.body: The changed `loginTotpStep1` value reads “Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare,” which is Italian rather than Lithuanian. Lithuanian users setting up an authenticator during login will see an unrelated-language instruction.

findings.title: The Simplified Chinese OTP instruction uses Traditional Chinese
findings.body: The replacement instruction uses Traditional Chinese characters and wording (`手機`, `應用程式`) in the `zh_CN` catalog. Simplified Chinese account users will receive a visibly mismatched translation during authenticator setup.
